description: Mapping extreme locations on Earth that serve as natural testbeds for permanent Moon and Mars habitats, with a focus on terrain similarity, radiation shielding, and human survival.
summary: ExoVitals combines an interactive Google Earth 3D explorer with a 40-point Space Medicine Site-Selection Index to match five extreme Earth environments—including Sri Lankan serpentine plains and hypersaline flats—with permanent Moon and Mars base locations based on radiation shielding, isolation physiology, and astrobiology.
details: Permanent human habitats on the Moon and Mars face severe biomedical hazards: ionizing cosmic radiation, extreme cold, psychological isolation, toxic regolith dust, and microbial contamination. While traditional planetary analog studies focus mainly on geology and rover testing, ExoVitals evaluates Earth analog locations through a Space Medicine and human survival lens. Using NASA Worldview satellite imagery and MODIS Land Surface Temperature data alongside NASA Moon Trek (LRO & Diviner) and NASA Mars Trek (PDS) terrain maps, we developed the ExoVitals Index—a 40-point scoring system grading sites across Radiation Shielding (R), Isolation Stress (I), Bio-Safety (B), and Terrain Stability (T), while explicitly documenting where each Earth analogy fails (such as gravity, vacuum, and atmospheric differences). We mapped five analog pairs inside a live 3D Google Earth tour: Ussangoda Serpentine Plain, Sri Lanka (Gusev Crater, Mars), Bundala/Hambantota Salterns, Sri Lanka (Terra Sirenum, Mars), Lava Beds National Monument, USA (Marius Hills Lava Tubes, Moon), Haughton Crater, Canada (Shackleton Crater, Lunar South Pole), and Atacama Desert, Chile (Jezero Crater, Mars). This tool helps flight surgeons and mission planners prioritize Earth training environments for long-duration human survival.
